newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Killer says he targeted Rabin as "terrorist".
newsitem.headline: Killer says he targeted Rabin as "terrorist".

text.p: The religious Jew who killed Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin to halt peace moves with the Arabs told a state inquiry into the assassination he felt he was shooting a "terrorist", an Israeli newspaper said on Thursday.

"When I fired I felt like I was firing at a terrorist," Yigal Amir said, according to the Yedioth Ahronoth daily, printing what it said were excerpts from his testimony. "I am unable to kill innocent people."
Ultra-nationalist Amir, 27, is serving a life sentence for shooting Rabin at a Tel Aviv peace rally on November 4, 1995, after stalking him for months.
Rabin shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994 for reaching an accord with PLO leader Yasser Arafat that launched Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
His assassination set Israel on a path to new elections in which right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ousted Rabin's Labour party.

Amir's mother Geula took her public struggle for her son to Israel's High Court of Justice on Thursday, demanding in a petition that his onetime friend Avishai Raviv be put on trial for coaxing her son into murdering Rabin.
A copy of the petition was faxed to Reuters.
Raviv, former leader of the shadowy right-wing Eyal group, was widely reported in Israel to be an informer for the Shin Bet security service.
Witnesses at Amir's trial said they heard Raviv goading Amir to go through with the murder. Police detained Raviv briefly after the assassination but never charged him.
